review_notes:
I read the whole theorem and the declarations it uses: exists_finite_disk_collar, path_near_endpoints, pathSubarc_range, polygonal_replacement_with_spurs, PolygonalChain.widen and isOpen_outsideDisks. The proof is a linear sequence of named steps (collars at both ends, endpoint parameters u and v, the path η = segment · subarc · segment, spur inclusions, then polygonal replacement). Each step has a clear mathematical role.

The only simplification candidates were small. The membership proofs for hA and hB could be written as one-line term-mode lambdas using Or.imp_right. The proof of hSU could use Set.insert_subset. The rw/dsimp in hη could become a simp only call. None of these removes a real redundancy, and each would make the term harder to read or merely change the style. I judged them to be personal taste, so I flagged nothing.
